transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-08
Start: 14:00 PT | Duration: ~56m
Recording: internal link
Participants: Sofia (Redwood AE), Derek (Redwood SE), Maya (Oriole Head ML), Carlos (CTO), Evan (SRE)

Summary:
Quick kickoff to scope a 2-week pilot focused on unit economics for Oriole's chat assistant workload. Discussed workload sizing, target benchmarks, per-token cost ballpark, batching and prefix/K V cache knobs, and a concrete benchmark plan. Agreed next steps and owners.

Topics:
- Success criteria and SLOs (P95 latency, throughput)
- Workload mix and sample traces needed
- Cost per token estimates and sensitivity to batch/cache/quantization
- Benchmark plan and timeline (2-week pilot)
- Security / VPC integration notes

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sofia Chen: All right hi everyone thanks for joining, um this is Sofia from Redwood, and with me is Derek our SE. uh we scheduled 45 minutes but looks like we have a little extra time so we'll be mindful.
[00:12] Maya Patel: Hi hi, thanks Sofia, appreciate it. I'll hand to Carlos to kick off with some context.
[00:18] Carlos Ruiz: Cool yeah, quick context — Oriole runs a customer support assistant and we're looking to move off an expensive in-house thing, we want predictable costs and lower latency for certain regions. key constraints: monthly budget cap ~USD 60k for inference, must keep P95 under 350ms for short queries, and SSO/SSO audit logs must be available.
[00:38] Derek Alvarez: Got it, thanks. Just to confirm, is that 350ms end-to-end or server-side? and what percent of requests are <128 tokens?
[00:45] Carlos Ruiz: That's end-to-end, and roughly 80% are short <100 token chat turns, the rest are longer, about 5% long form >512 tokens.
[00:53] Evan Meyer: And we have a VPC — we'll need to understand VPC peering timing, but we can open a peering window in the next two weeks.
[01:05] Sofia Chen: Perfect. So the scope of the pilot we're proposing: a focused benchmarking sprint to (1) validate per-token unit economics with your traffic mix, (2) test batching and prefix caching to see cost/latency tradeoffs, and (3) give a recommended config for production or Redwood Dedicated if necessary.
[01:24] Maya Patel: Sounds good. I want a clear success criteria doc — how do we measure cost per active user?
[01:30] Derek Alvarez: We'll map trace-level metrics to per-req and per-token cost. rough back of the napkin numbers: for hosted inference on a small LLaMA-class model at q4 quantization maybe ~ $0.0007 per 1 token? sorry that's muddled — let me be clearer: about $0.7 per 1k tokens as a baseline on hosted with minimal batching, and down to $0.15-$0.3 per 1k tokens with aggressive batching, prefix/K V cache, and quantization on the right hardware. these are illustrative and we'll run your trace through the harness to get real numbers.
[02:05] Carlos Ruiz: Wait $0.7 per 1k tokens is high, our current internal average is about $0.5k token equivalent, so we need to see savings. What are the knobs you tune?
[02:16] Derek Alvarez: The main levers: batching (grouping concurrent requests to amortize overhead), KV/prefix caching to avoid recomputing common prefixes, and quantization (int8/4bit) to reduce GPU runtime cost. Also model variant routing — lighter model for short queries, fallback to bigger model for long ones. We also consider reserved capacity (Dedicated) to reduce unit cost when steady throughput exists.
[02:34] Maya Patel: For batching, do you set a max latency threshold? like don't batch beyond x ms?
[02:39] Derek Alvarez: Yes, we do dynamic batching with latency SLO windows. e.g., max hold 8–12ms for latency sensitive routes, but you can tune to higher holds if you want lower cost. In practice we've seen batch sizes of 4–16 for chat workloads depending on concurrency.
[02:53] Evan Meyer: Our concurrency is bursty — sometimes 300 QPS for a few minutes.
[02:58] Derek Alvarez: Ok that maps to autoscale and burst capacity discussion. For the pilot we'll simulate your burst trace to validate autoscale and tail latencies.
[03:08] Carlos Ruiz: On caching: how often do you see prefix reuse? for us many queries start with the same system prompt and are short continuations.
[03:14] Derek Alvarez: If the system prompt + user prefix repeats, K V caching can hit a lot — sometimes 25–40% token skip on average for support use cases. But depends on prompt engineering and whether you do retrieval-augmented prompts.
[03:25] Sofia Chen: quick note on numbers — Derek's $0.7/1k was conservative, we'll run your traces and produce a per-scenario table (short chat, long chat, docs summarize). we'll put per-token and per-request estimates in the pricing worksheet.
[03:40] Maya Patel: Great. What does the benchmark look like?
[03:44] Derek Alvarez: Plan is: you upload 48h of traces (anonymized); we run three benchmark passes: (A) baseline host config (no caching, small batch), (B) caching + tuned batching + quantization variants, (C) production-like routing with fallback model variants. Each pass will collect latency distribution (P50/P95/P99), throughput, token counts, and estimated $/1k token. We aim to run the full suite in a 2–4 hour window but we'll do iterative runs to debug.
[04:09] Carlos Ruiz: And timeline?
[04:11] Sofia Chen: Ideal is: traces + success criteria by 9/9, benchmark run week of 9/13, analysis and config recommendations by 9/17, pilot SOW signed and pilot start 9/20. That's aggressive but doable.
[04:24] Maya Patel: Works for us.
[04:26] Evan Meyer: On the security side — we need SOC2 docs and KMS/HSM options.
[04:31] Derek Alvarez: Yes we'll share SOC2 whitepaper and our KMS integration notes. For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS and a private control plane.
[04:41] Carlos Ruiz: Any gotchas with our on-prem data egress limits? we have tight policies for EU customers.
[04:46] Derek Alvarez: We can run the pilot in a region close to your users and we also have on-prem package options. For the benchmark we can run in your preferred region — just note network egress affects latency numbers.
[04:58] Maya Patel: Let's talk success criteria in detail. I want to propose: (1) P95 server-side latency < 250ms for short queries, (2) cost per MAU < $0.40 per active user/month at current usage patterns, (3) no regression on quality measured by our 200-case regression set.
[05:18] Derek Alvarez: that's specific, which is great. We'll map your regression set runs to the config matrix. For the cost per MAU we need to clarify your MAU definition and tokens per MAU; we'll convert trace totals to per-MAU token spend.
[05:31] Maya Patel: We'll provide the MAU calc in the success doc.
[05:34] Sofia Chen: Awesome. A few practical notes: we'll provide a benchmark harness (link: https://redwood.example/bench-harness) — that's a short link. Derek will include default configs: batch windows 8ms/15ms, batch max 16, prefix cache TTL 30s default, quant options: int8 and 4bit ranges.
[05:55] Derek Alvarez: Also we'll snapshot model cost curves: hosted per-token at various batch & cache combos, and compare to Dedicated reserved node pricing (committed monthly) to show break-even. ballpark break-even for steady throughput is often 2–3 months depending on concurrency.
[06:10] Carlos Ruiz: Can you share an example table?
[06:13] Derek Alvarez: Yes we'll include a small example in the worksheet: short chat (avg 40 tokens) - no batch = $0.9/1k, with batch+cache = $0.18/1k; long chat (avg 600 tokens) - no batch = $2.1/1k, with batching = $0.6/1k. again illustrative.
[06:30] Maya Patel: The numbers swing a lot; what's the sensitivity to concurrency?
[06:33] Derek Alvarez: Highly sensitive. More concurrency -> larger batches -> lower amortized per-request overhead. But you hit diminishing returns once GPU is saturated. That's why we run your trace to capture real concurrency distribution.
[06:45] Evan Meyer: Anything about quantization affecting quality?
[06:48] Derek Alvarez: Yes quantization can introduce small degradations; we'll run your regression set across quantized model variants to measure impact. That's part of the pass B.
[06:58] Sofia Chen: Cool. I'm going to summarize next steps now.
[07:02] Sofia Chen: Derek will share the harness and default config, Sofia will send the pilot SOW and price worksheet, Oriole will upload traces and success criteria doc. we'll run the benchmark week of 9/13 and aim to deliver results by 9/17.
[07:17] Carlos Ruiz: One more question: If we need private deployment later, how much lead time?
[07:21] Derek Alvarez: Private (VPC/on-prem) provisioning is typically 4–8 weeks depending on compliance work and networking windows. We'll surface that in the SOW as an optional path.
[07:33] Maya Patel: Ok, thanks.
[07:35] Sofia Chen: Thanks everyone. we'll follow up with an email and attach the workshop checklist and links.

[37:10] (noise - brief interruption, folks rejoin)
[40:02] Derek Alvarez: Quick deep-dive note — measurement approach for per-token cost: we'll combine token accounting from model runtime with infra-hourly cost. For hosted runs you see per-inference overhead (init, scheduling) that batching reduces; for Dedicated it's more about utilization percent. We'll output both per-token and per-invocation buckets.
[44:20] Maya Patel: I saw mention of K V cache TTL — if we set TTL to 30s does that have memory growth?
[44:28] Derek Alvarez: Yes memory is bounded by active prefix set; cache eviction and TTL tuning included in recommendations.
[47:05] Carlos Ruiz: For the benchmark, can you simulate our fallback routing (small model for short, big for long)?
[47:12] Derek Alvarez: Yes that's pass C. We'll provide a routing policy file and simulate that behavior.
[50:00] Evan Meyer: On instrumentation — can you send the set of metrics you'll need? we'll add Redwoods tracing hooks to our telemetry.
[50:07] Derek Alvarez: We'll send a metrics spec: per-request tokens, model variant used, GPU occupancy, batch sizes, queue latency, and KV cache hit rates.
[50:18] Sofia Chen: Great, final recap in the notes after the call. Thanks again.

Closing notes:
- Tone: technical/operational, AE + SE pairing.
- Benchmarks to include: latency distributions, token counts, cache hit rates, cost per 1k tokens, break-even Dedicated analysis.
- Pilot length: 2-week engagement (trace collection, benchmark runs, config recommendations) with option to extend into a 60–90 day pilot on Dedicated if results justify it.

References / links shared during call:
- Bench harness: https://redwood.example/bench-harness
- Pilot SOW template (to be attached by Sofia)
- Security pack (SOC2 + KMS notes) (to be attached)

End of transcript.
